title: The Lord has spoken to Malachi
html_source:
A little blasphemy from Malachi “Buck” Mulligan.

The biblical Book of Malachi is constructed as God’s message to the people of Israel through the prophet. The book opens thusly (Mal 1:1-3):

The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by Malachi.
“I have loved you,” saith the Lord.
Yet ye say, “Wherein hast thou loved us?”
“Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” saith the Lord, “yet I loved Jacob. And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.”

Not only is this bit of scripture structured as a dialogue, as is much of this chapter of Ulysses, it observes the Esau/Jacob conflict to which Stephen has recently alluded.
